title: a-ticket-is-a-list-of-decisions-not-prose

decisions.text: A ticket is a list of one-line decisions, each carrying who made it. Big decisions go to intentions; small ones go on the ticket.
decisions.by: Akien verbatim 2026-09-15: 'less prose, more decisions made ... yeah, we have some big ones, but they need to be in our intentions. small ones need to be in the ticket.'

decisions.text: The prose ticket-v1 copies onto the ticket (why, how, cast_checks, challenge_at_birth) stays in the berths it came from and is pointed at, never repeated.
decisions.by: derived from CLAUDE.md Law 5 (the key points, not the trail) and Law 7 (the berths keep the prose; nothing is collapsed)

decisions.text: ticket-v2 is compiled from a census over the rehearsal records' decision lines, never authored first. The census is a COUNT, not an extraction (there is no 'noun a line settles' to identify). Its algorithm, run 2026-09-16 over 16 records (the ten required are met): for every record under CairnCommons/rehearsals/ open the ticket it names and read decisions[]; count (a) each key a decision line carries and how many lines carry it — measured n 70, text 70, by 70, step 37, source 37, amended 5, folded_text 4; (b) each line's by-kind from its leading words — measured 'Akien verbatim' 22, 'CC at cast' 4, 'CC under rehearsal' 20, 'derived from' 3, unlabeled 21; (c) each gap's step, a D-line id or a prose step — measured 69 D-lines, 72 prose; (d) per ticket, which prose fields are present — intention, why, how, traces_to, cast_checks, challenge_at_birth on all four. Schema rule from the counts: a key on every line is required (n, text, by); a key on every line added under rehearsal is required for such lines (step, source); a key that appears only on revision is optional (amended, folded_text); the prose fields the gaps name as steps are dropped (D6's list). WHERE THE CENSUS DATA IS: before this build it is the measurement file /tmp/claude-1000/-home-akien-dev-src-cairn/a187d6ab-5944-4bda-9405-365b2b200f92/scratchpad/census_v2.json (absolute path; measured 2026-09-16 21:59 to exist, 1 file, sha256 4b8e394bfe8d9602ceb17e8f3859735f6af414c8e92a879ed1b0ddd5e1d3ae79; the build's FIRST act is to read it — if it is absent or its sha differs the build is RED and stops, and nothing re-measures: a re-measurement is a new census on a new day and needs a new decision line, never an improvised step; a JSON object with keys measured, by, records, gap_kinds, gap_step_shape, decision_line_keys, by_kinds, tickets, per_record, reading); the build copies that object verbatim into CairnCommons/tickets/_schema-v2.json under the key census, and that file is committed to the CairnCommons git repo, so every later builder reads the census from git and never from a scratchpad. A rerun on a later day is a python3 script implementing steps (a)-(d) over CairnCommons/rehearsals/*.json and the tickets they name — no LLM — and the schema file's census.how carries that one-paragraph algorithm so the rerun needs nothing else.

decisions.text: Every decision line carries a `by` in one of four shapes — 'Akien verbatim <date>', 'derived from <address>', 'CC at cast <date>', 'CC under rehearsal <record>' — and the door refuses a line without one. IMPLEMENTATION: a judge inside judge_packet in skills/sorted/door.py, riding the one refusal every other lack rides: for each element of the packet's decisions list, append a lack {field: 'decisions', why: 'line <n>: <what is wrong>'} unless the element is a dict carrying n (int), text (non-empty str) and by (str) whose by starts with one of the four prefixes 'Akien verbatim ', 'derived from ', 'CC at cast ', 'CC under rehearsal ' (prefix match, case-sensitive); every offending line is named, not only the first; an empty or absent decisions list is the flat contract's lack (the seam reads every contract field as required and non-empty) and is not reported twice. Lines the rehearsal machine adds later with --decide carry by 'CC' plus step and source 'rehearsal'; they are post-cast lines the door never sees, and the schema names that pair as the 'CC under rehearsal <record>' shape's realisation — no edit to the rehearsal machine.

decisions.text: Ticket filing moves into skills/sorted/door.py: the sorted door files the ticket it berths, and the caster writes no ticket by hand and no filing script (today filing is a scratchpad script rewritten each voyage — file_tickets.py 2026-09-14, file_tickets2.py 2026-09-15, castlib.py 2026-09-16 — the measured gap). BUILD ORDER inside this one voyage: first the charter skills/sorted/intention+why.json gains the two contract fields decisions and intent_berth (that is D15's act, done before any line of door.py is edited); then file_ticket is written. The check that the two fields are present and non-empty is NOT new code: the standing seam cairn/machines/learning_block/learning_block.py:219 inspect_input already refuses any contract field that is absent or empty, so adding the fields to the charter IS the check — the only new judge in door.py is the by check on each line (D4). THE INPUT is the sorted packet, which after that charter change ALWAYS carries decisions (a list of lines) and intent_berth (the absolute path of the /intent berth) — both required, non-empty, refused by name when absent. THE FUNCTION is file_ticket(payload, berth, *, commons) in door.py, called from fire() after sb.fire returns and only when payload['exit'] == 'routed_forward' (a routed_out packet berths and files nothing): it reads from_idea and task_or_ticket out of the intent berth's answers; mints the id as secrets.token_hex(6), redrawn while a file <hex>-* already stands in the tickets store; builds the v2 ticket from the packet's own fields — id, title, node_class, task_or_ticket, workflow_and_state (the packet's workflow), date and created (today), author ('CC via /sorted'), from_idea, intent_berth, sorted_berth (= result['berth'], the path sb.fire returned), owner (the packet's gates_bound owner if named, else 'CC'), owning_intention (the packet's owning_intention if present, else the title), questions (the packet's questions), falsifier (the packet's falsifier_check), watchme, depends_on ([]), follow_ons (the packet's children unless it is a 'none, because' string, then []), schema_version 'ticket-v2', rehearsal 'none-yet', decisions (the packet's list verbatim); writes <hex>-<title>.json under <commons>/tickets/ through cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write(path, json text, verb='cast', why='/sorted cast <hex> <title>: sorted berth <berth>') — 'cast' is the verb every ticket write already journals under; commons is the injected kwarg fire() already accepts (the proof's scratch commons) or, when None, the live commons the door's other judges default to (_COMMONS). THE OUTPUT: the dict fire() returns gains ticket_path (absolute) and ticket_id (the hex), and main() prints it as it prints the berth today.

`cairn operator show artifact <id>` renders a v2 ticket on one screen, and a v1 ticket still loads and renders. WHERE: the edit is inside _format_ticket in cairn/tools/operator_inbox/inbox.py and nowhere else in the renderer; show_artifact's resolution (pending berth first, then the ticket by id prefix under TICKETS_DIR) is untouched. THE READER: a new function ticket_version(doc) in inbox.py returns 'v2' iff str(doc.get('schema_version') or '').startswith('ticket-v2') else 'v1'. ONE SCREEN: at most 60 lines at width 76, asserted by a tooth. SECTION ORDER for v2, nothing else printed: the standing header (the '=' rule, TICKET id, title, class/state, path, '=' rule, blank); INTENTION: — owning_intention printed as an address, one line, two-space indent; DECISIONS: — one entry per line as '<n>. <text> [<by>]' wrapped at 76 with a two-space hang (_wrap with indent '  '); QUESTIONS: — the standing _questions_tree, only when it renders non-empty; BERTHS: — three lines 'intent_berth: <path>', 'sorted_berth: <path>', 'chart_claim: <the latest validate berth claiming the ticket, or none>'. For v1 the intention/what/why/how loop and the FALSIFIER, DEPENDENCIES, MEASUREMENTS and QUESTIONS sections stay exactly as they are; a v1 ticket gains a DECISIONS section (same format, placed after MEASUREMENTS and before QUESTIONS) only when it carries a non-empty decisions[]; a v1 ticket without decisions renders byte-identical to the pre-edit renderer.

decisions.text: The schema file CairnCommons/tickets/_schema-v2.json is one JSON object with exactly three top-level keys: schema_version (the string 'ticket-v2'), schema, and census (the D3 measurement copied in verbatim, plus census.how, the one-paragraph rerun algorithm). schema is an object mapping each kept field to its one-line meaning, spelled here so nothing is inferred: id — the 12-hex ticket identifier minted at cast; title — the slug the file is named by (<id>-<title>.json); node_class — the class in CairnCommons/node_classes/ (e.g. code-seam); task_or_ticket — 'ticket' or 'task' as /intent answered it; workflow_and_state — the rendered workflow string with its cursor in brackets; date and created — the cast date, ISO yyyy-mm-dd; author — who cast it (e.g. 'CC (Opus 5), session <id>'); from_idea — the id under CairnCommons/ideas/ or 'none, because <X>'; intent_berth — absolute path of the /intent berth; sorted_berth — absolute path of the /sorted berth; owner — who gates writes to the component (a charter address or a name); owning_intention — the charter or homeless-intention address the ticket serves; questions — list of open-<id> question ids or 'none, because <X>'; falsifier — the one prose field kept, the done/wrong-intent test; watchme — the WATCHME spec object or 'none, because <X>'; depends_on — list of ticket ids or texts this ticket waits on; follow_ons — list of child ticket ids or first-cut names; schema_version — 'ticket-v2'; rehearsal — the latest rehearsal record path or 'none-yet'; decisions — a list of {n (int, 1-based), text (one line), by (provenance, one of the four shapes) required; step and source required on a line added under rehearsal; amended and folded_text optional}. Nothing in the file is authored beyond these one-line meanings; the field set is D6's list as the census confirmed it.

intention: A ticket is a list of one-line decisions, each carrying who made it, and never a body of prose: the big decisions live in intentions, the small ones on the ticket, and the reader who cannot infer (Akien, Haiku) can scan it.
why: Law 5 (the address carries what a mind needs NOW, the key points not the trail — a ticket's prose is the trail); Law 1 (compile the settled: the schema is compiled from what rehearsals actually asked, not authored ahead of evidence); CP4 designing to the tool where the tool is now two readers, Akien's 'ADD brain' and the cheapest model, neither of whom infers from prose (Akien 2026-09-15: 'i read many of your tickets and i just get lost in the verbage ... less prose, more decisions made').
how: ticket-v2, precipitated rather than designed: after the rehearsal (its sibling ticket) has run over at least ten real tickets, the decision kinds that recurred become the schema — id, title, the intention it serves (a charter or homeless-intention address), decisions[] each {text: one line, by: 'Akien verbatim <date>' | 'derived from <address>' | 'CC under rehearsal <record>'}, falsifier, questions, rehearsal, workflow_and_state, and the three berth addresses. The prose that ticket-v1 copies onto the ticket (why, how, cast_checks, challenge_at_birth) stays in the berths it came from and is pointed at, not repeated. `cairn operator show artifact` renders decisions as a list he can veto a line of. Existing tickets are not migrated by hand; an open v1 ticket becomes v2 by being rehearsed (each gap answered is a decision line). The boundary big/small: a decision that changes a charter's what or why is big and goes to the intention in the same act.
falsifier: DONE when, measured by the sorted door's proofs (skills/sorted/proofs/) and the renderer's (cairn/tools/operator_inbox/proofs/): (1) ticket-v2 is written from a census over the first ten rehearsal records' decision lines, the census stored beside the schema; (2) the sorted door files a v2 ticket with decisions[] where every line carries a by in {Akien verbatim <date>, derived from <address>, CC under rehearsal <record>} and no prose field; (3) `cairn operator show artifact <id>` renders decisions as a numbered list, the berths as addresses; (4) a v1 ticket still loads and renders; (5) Akien reads one v2 ticket and reports he could follow it (his words, recorded as the answer to a question on this ticket).
